Question:
Find the sum of the digits in the answer to

\[\underbrace{9999\cdots99}_{94} \times \underbrace{4444\cdots44}_{94}\]

where a string of \(94\) nines is multiplied by a string of \(94\) fours.
Solution:
The string of 94 nines is \(10^{94}-1\). Let \(F\) be the number consisting of 94 fours. Multiplication by \(10^{94}\) appends 94 zeros, so the required product is
\[
F(10^{94}-1)=F10^{94}-F.
\]
To identify its digits, borrow one unit from the block before those 94 zeros:
\[
F10^{94}-F
=(F-1)10^{94}+(10^{94}-F).
\]
The first block, \(F-1\), consists of 93 fours followed by a 3.

For the second block, first subtract \(F\) from the string of 94 nines. Each column gives \(9-4=5\), with no borrowing. Adding 1 then gives
\[
10^{94}-F
=\underbrace{55\cdots5}_{94}+1
=\underbrace{55\cdots5}_{93}6.
\]
This second block has exactly 94 digits and is less than \(10^{94}\), so it fits after the first block without any further carrying.

The product therefore has 93 fours, a 3, 93 fives, and a 6. Its digit sum is
\[
93\cdot4+3+93\cdot5+6
=93\cdot9+9
=\boxed{846},
\]
choice \(\text{A}\).
